body: Tanzania has extremely limited coverage, including several Generation 3 trekkers in Gombe National Park and tripods on Mount Kilimanjaro. Some spill coverage made by a regular Google car exists on the Kenya border, but trekkers and tripods are typically off-road and not useful for serious mapping or territory identification.

On Mount Kilimanjaro, there are a couple of tripods—that is, cameras mounted on tripods—providing coverage with a distinct ethereal look, including motion blur and slightly saturated colors. Tripods appear in other countries as well.
Mount Kilimanjaro tripods show a high altitude landscape with dark grey rock and eternal snow in places, sometimes including mountaineers and tents.
A walking trekker covers much of Gombe National Park, with dense jungle and typically little sunlight in lowland areas, sometimes showing chimpanzees.
Higher hillsides in Gombe feature more open forest with savannah-like trees around.
Hilltops in Gombe have bare grasslands offering breathtaking views of the surrounding landscape and Lake Tanganyika.

A boat trekker on Lake Tanganyika hugs the coast near Gombe National Park, with the coast to the east and hills covered mostly by tropical forest. The boat is olive green and white, with pixelated people due to blur. Do not confuse it with boats in Madagascar.
Another tripod is located inside Jane Goodall’s house in Gombe National Park, adjacent to standard Generation 3 trekker coverage.
